text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Telecommunication group Tele Danmark and Norwegian media group Shibsted have been negotiating for almost a year with film company Metronome in an effort to acquire a majority stake in the company. If Tele Danmark and Shibsted take over Metronome it is to be split up into different units for TV and film production, foreign film rights, video distribution and cinemas.
--- A new United Nations centre is to be opened on October 7 in Copenhagen. The centre is to house several UN agencies, with a total of 150 employees.

--- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) has received a large number of complaints since it prohibited smoking on short-haul European flights. So far SAS has no plans of allowing smoking again and the new rules will therefore affect most of the 19 million passengers who go with SAS each year.

--- For the first time in many years fewer people want to join the police. In the first six months of 1996 the police report almost 20 percent fewer applicants than 1995 when about 1000 people wanted to get into the police force. The police are now considering hiring a recruiting campaign to avoid a lack of new qualified police officers in years to come.

--- French construction company S.D.E.M which is building the fixed Great Belt bridge and tunnel connection has been reported to the police for the third time now after the latest accidential death on the construction in the beginning of September. So far nine construction workers have died during the construction.
--- The lifting of retail shopping hour restrictions has moved trade worth millions of crowns from small kiosks and neighbourhood stores to the big retail chains.
